judgments.title: Arbitration Opt-Out Notice Uses Wrong Entity Name and Excludes Lender
judgments.reason: The opt-out provision's use of “PLS Financial Services” conflicts with the agreement's identification of “PLS Loan Store of Texas, Inc.” as the contracting CAB. The additional failure to require notice to DSI is merely an omission, but the entity mismatch is the closer construction defect.

judgments.title: Comma Splice Creates Ambiguity in Loan Disclaimer
judgments.reason: The comma splice is a grammatical error, but the two independent propositions remain readily separable and their meaning is not changed.

judgments.title: Lender Identification Incomplete
judgments.reason: DSI Lending Resources, Inc. is expressly identified by name. Omission of additional corporate or licensing details is a disclosure concern, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: DSI Not Identified as Party or Third-Party Beneficiary
judgments.reason: DSI is not a signatory or expressly designated beneficiary, yet multiple operative provisions purport to confer rights on or impose arbitration and waiver terms involving “Lender.” Reading those provisions together raises a whole-instrument question about DSI's contractual status and enforcement rights.

judgments.title: Missing space after period
judgments.reason: The source text contains a comma splice rather than the alleged missing space after a period. Although grammatically defective, it does not change the meaning of the two propositions.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Lender
judgments.reason: In “we are not a lender,” lowercase “lender” is used as a common noun describing PLS's role, whereas capitalized “Lender” identifies DSI. The distinction is coherent rather than ambiguous.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Credit Services Agreement
judgments.reason: The document is titled “Credit Services Agreement” and initially defines it as the “Agreement,” so the governing-law reference plainly identifies this instrument.

judgments.title: Entire Agreement Clause Lacks Survival Language
judgments.reason: The clause's failure expressly to address electronic writings and signatures is an omitted clarification, not an ambiguity or conflict.

judgments.title: Modification Requires Only Customer and CAB Signatures — Lender Excluded
judgments.reason: The modification clause unambiguously requires signatures from the customer and PLS. Whether DSI should also have consent rights is a legal or commercial concern, not an internal textual inconsistency.

judgments.title: Bankruptcy Warranty May Be Unenforceable
judgments.reason: The issue concerns enforceability under federal bankruptcy policy rather than ambiguity, mechanical error, or conflict within the instrument.

judgments.title: Data Sharing Authorization Lacks Service Provider Coverage
judgments.reason: The authorization's failure to include service providers, successors, and assigns is a desired expansion of rights, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Notice of Cancellation
judgments.reason: The two attached forms are each headed “Notice of Cancellation,” making the acknowledgment's reference clear without a separate formal definition.

judgments.title: Typo - improper character
judgments.reason: The “¢” character is an erroneous list marker, but the surrounding warranties remain grammatically and substantively understandable, so it does not change the provision's meaning.

judgments.title: Information Sharing Authorization Limited to "Duration of Services"
judgments.reason: The issue seeks to extend the authorization beyond the service period for collection and compliance purposes. It does not identify competing reasonable meanings or an internal conflict.

neg31.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — How to Cancel
neg31.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Redundant Entity Name in Cancellation Notice Address
judgments.reason: Repeating the same entity name in the address is untidy but does not change the recipient or otherwise alter the provision's meaning.

judgments.title: Same Redundancy in Second Notice of Cancellation
judgments.reason: The duplicate entity name in the second cancellation form is redundant formatting that does not change the address or substantive meaning.

judgments.title: Ambiguous Prepayment Refund Scope
judgments.reason: The phrase “for the final period” has an uncertain temporal scope and could mean the installment period in which prepayment occurs or the remaining loan term.

judgments.title: Tension Between "Irrevocable" LOC and Automatic Revocation
judgments.reason: Calling the LOC “irrevocable” conflicts facially with the operative provision automatically revoking it upon timely cancellation, even though the latter could be construed as an exception.

judgments.title: Typo - "Joan" should be "loan"
judgments.reason: “Joan payments” is an erroneous substitution for “loan payments,” literally changing the referenced type of payment to nonsensical language.

judgments.title: Missing space before dollar amount
judgments.reason: The corrupted text “ofS” fails clearly to present the intended dollar sign and amount field for the CAB fee, mechanically obscuring the financial disclosure.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Amount Financed
judgments.reason: “Amount Financed” is a standard consumer-credit concept and is used as the label for a transaction-specific amount. Capitalization without a bespoke definition does not itself create genuine ambiguity.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Finance Charge
judgments.reason: The agreement expressly states that the Finance Charge consists of lender interest and the CAB fee. The alleged lack of definition therefore does not create a construction issue.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Annual Percentage Rate
judgments.reason: “Annual Percentage Rate” is a standard statutory credit term whose absence from a definitions section does not make its meaning genuinely uncertain.

judgments.title: Missing annualized rate percentage
judgments.reason: The annualized-rate field is unfilled, mechanically omitting the percentage needed to calculate the CAB fee.

judgments.title: Unfilled loan principal amount
judgments.reason: The blank principal field omits the transaction's loan amount and consequently leaves a central payment obligation incomplete.

judgments.title: Unfilled number of payments
judgments.reason: The blank installment-count field is a mechanical omission that prevents the payment schedule from specifying how many payments are due.

judgments.title: Missing Amount Financed
judgments.reason: The Amount Financed field is blank, mechanically omitting the dollar value to which the surrounding payment terms refer.

judgments.title: Missing Finance Charge
judgments.reason: The Finance Charge field is unfilled, leaving the stated total cost of credit mechanically incomplete.

judgments.title: Unfilled lender interest amount
judgments.reason: The lender-interest component contains an unfilled dollar field, mechanically omitting part of the stated Finance Charge breakdown.

judgments.title: Missing first payment date and amount
judgments.reason: The first payment date and amount are both blank, leaving the commencement of the repayment schedule mechanically incomplete.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Total of Payments
judgments.reason: “Total of Payments” is a standard credit-disclosure label used for the stated aggregate payment amount. No competing contractual meaning is identified.

judgments.title: Payment Waterfall Disadvantages Lender
judgments.reason: The payment waterfall expressly states the order of application. Its commercial disadvantage to the lender is a negotiation issue, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: CAB Fee Prorated Rebate Only for "Final Period" — Narrow Scope
judgments.reason: “For the final period” has an uncertain temporal scope and could refer either to the installment period containing payoff or more broadly to the remaining loan term.

judgments.title: Spacing error
judgments.reason: The text “ofS” mechanically corrupts the intended dollar sign and amount field for the CAB fee, obscuring that financial disclosure.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Amount Financed
judgments.reason: “Amount Financed” is a standard consumer-credit label for the disclosed transaction amount. The lack of a separate formal definition does not itself produce competing meanings.

judgments.title: Unfilled annualized rate
judgments.reason: The annualized CAB-fee rate field is unfilled, mechanically omitting a value necessary to calculate the fee.

judgments.title: Unfilled number of payments
judgments.reason: The blank payment-count field mechanically leaves the number of required installments unspecified.

judgments.title: Unfilled Amount Financed with trailing comma
judgments.reason: The Amount Financed field is blank, so the transaction-specific dollar amount is mechanically absent.

judgments.title: Unfilled Finance Charge amount
judgments.reason: The Finance Charge field is unfilled, mechanically omitting the disclosed total cost of credit.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Annual Percentage Rate
judgments.reason: “Annual Percentage Rate” is a standard statutory consumer-credit term and is not rendered ambiguous merely because the contract lacks a separate definition.

judgments.title: Undefined term: CAB Fee
judgments.reason: The context identifies the CAB fee as the fee PLS charges for its listed credit-access services and states its calculation basis. A formal defined-term provision is unnecessary to understand the reference.

judgments.title: Undefined term: State Allowed Returned Item Fee
judgments.reason: Read with the Texas governing-law clause, “State Allowed Returned Item Fee” objectively refers to the returned-item fee allowed by applicable Texas law. The absence of a fixed amount does not make it genuinely indeterminate.

judgments.title: Reimbursement Interest Rate May Be Below Market for Default
judgments.reason: The 10% reimbursement rate is definite. Whether it is economically adequate for post-default risk is a negotiation question.

judgments.title: Undefined term: State Allowed Returned Item Fee
judgments.reason: Together with the Texas governing-law clause, the phrase objectively points to the returned-item fee permitted by applicable Texas law. Failure to state a fixed amount is not a genuine textual ambiguity.

judgments.title: Spelling - "unlgyuful" should be "unlawful"
judgments.reason: “Unlgyuful” is a corrupted spelling of “unlawful” that turns an operative condition into a nonexistent word, although the intended word is inferable.

judgments.title: LOC 10-Day Default Waiting Period Delays Lender Recovery
judgments.reason: The ten-day waiting period is definite and internally consistent. The desire for faster LOC recovery is purely commercial.

judgments.title: LOC Described as "Irrevocable" but Subject to Automatic Revocation
judgments.reason: The operative description of the LOC as “irrevocable” conflicts facially with its automatic revocation upon timely cancellation, requiring the cancellation provision to be construed as an exception.

judgments.title: LOC Coverage Omits Attorneys' Fees and Collection Costs
judgments.reason: The LOC may secure only a defined subset of the customer's broader lender obligations without contradiction. Adding attorneys' fees and collection costs would expand security rather than resolve ambiguity.

judgments.title: Corrupted text - typo in "unlawful"
judgments.reason: “Unlgyuful” is a mechanical misspelling that replaces the operative word “unlawful” with nonsense, even though the intended meaning is inferable.

judgments.title: Garbled text - nonsense phrase
judgments.reason: “Maximug peepee” is garbled text that prevents the clause from stating the intended maximum-lawful-rate limitation coherently.

judgments.title: Default Trigger for Lender Obligations May Be Overly Broad
judgments.reason: “Your obligations to the Lender” broadly but clearly encompasses the customer's lender obligations. The concern is overbreadth or unconscionability, not competing meanings.

judgments.title: Default Remedies Limited to CAB — No Express Lender Remedies
judgments.reason: The default clause's failure to grant the Lender parallel remedies is an omission of desired rights, not an ambiguity or conflict with another provision.

judgments.title: Incomplete sentence with annotation marker
judgments.reason: The corrupted phrase “maximug peepee” is a mechanical drafting error that replaces the intended legal limitation with nonsensical text and obscures the sentence's meaning.

pos1.clause_name: Definition of Claim — Arbitration Agreement and Limitation on Class Participation
pos1.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: agreement
judgments.reason: Lowercase “credit services agreement” appears within a broad list covering current agreements, loans, and obligations. The capitalization choice does not create a genuine ambiguity.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: arbitration agreement
judgments.reason: In context, lowercase “this arbitration agreement” plainly refers to the arbitration provision being stated. The capitalization inconsistency is stylistic only.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Agreement
judgments.reason: Lowercase “credit services agreement” occurs in a broad category within the Claim definition and does not necessarily purport to use the defined term “Agreement.” No genuine ambiguity results.

pos2.clause_name: Starting an Arbitration/Costs — election to arbitrate any Claim
pos2.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Arbitrator Selection Fallback Controlled by CAB
judgments.reason: The selection mechanism clearly gives the stated fallback authority to PLS. DSI's lack of a role is an omitted right rather than a construction defect.
